title: Local constant finite-module model for bounded cohomology on a site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with final object $X$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $K\in D(\mathcal C,\underline B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and integers $a\leq b$ satisfy $H^q(K)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Suppose every $H^q(K)$ is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. There exists a covering $\{U_j\to X\}$ such that on each localized site $\mathcal C/U_j$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], $K|_{U_j}$ is isomorphic in the derived category to the termwise constant sheaf complex $\underline{M_j^\bullet}$, where $M_j^\bullet$ is a cochain complex of finitely generated $B$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $M_j^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. The differentials of $\underline{M_j^\bullet}$ are induced by the $B$-linear differentials of $M_j^\bullet$. No existence of points of the site is assumed.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, the strengthened constant-model assertion explicitly proved in its induction

proof.text: Induct on $b-a$, with the claim for every small site with final object and every object having the stated interval and locally constant finite cohomology. Restriction to a slice is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; hence it preserves cohomology, quasi-isomorphisms, and cone triangles termwise. Constant sheaves restrict canonically to constant sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction]. Coverings on successive slices compose by the site axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. These facts allow each subsequent finite refinement and each application of the induction hypothesis on a slice. On an object covered by the empty sieve every module sheaf is zero, so the zero module complex is a model there; such objects may be treated separately throughout.

If $a=b$, take any complex representing $K$ and first replace it by its canonical upper truncation in degree $a$. The map to $H^a(K)[-a]$ is the projection from cycles in degree $a$, zero below; it is a quasi-isomorphism since the other cohomology vanishes. The upper truncation maps quasi-isomorphically to $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends]. Trivialize $H^a(K)$ on a covering as in the hypothesis and put that finite module in degree $a$. This includes $H^a(K)=0$.

Suppose $a<b$. Refine so $H^b(K)=\underline M$ for a finite $B$-module $M$, and choose generators $x_1,\ldots,x_r$. Represent $K$ by a complex $A$ with $A^q=0$ for $q>b$ using upper truncation [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends]. Let $Z^b=\ker(d_A^b)$. The quotient $Z^b\twoheadrightarrow H^b(A)$ is the sheafification of the presheaf quotient of $Z^b$ by the presheaf image of $d_A^{b-1}$: this follows from exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. The local representative assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] therefore lifts each of the finitely many sections $x_i$ to a cycle $z_i\in Z^b(U)$ after a finite sequence of covering refinements. Sending the $i$th basis vector to $z_i$, then sheafifying the natural constant-presheaf map, gives a chain map $P=\underline{B^r}[-b]\to A$ inducing the given surjection $\underline{B^r}\twoheadrightarrow\underline M$. This supplies explicitly the local lifting hidden under “details omitted” in the source, without hypercohomology or points.

Take the actual mapping cone $L=C(P\to A)$, so $P\to K\to L\xrightarrow{\delta}P[1]$ is distinguished [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] and surjectivity in degree $b$ give $H^q(L)=0$ outside $[a,b-1]$, $H^q(L)=H^q(K)$ for $q\le b-2$, and $0\to H^{b-1}(K)\to H^{b-1}(L)\to\ker(\underline{B^r}\to\underline M)\to0$. The kernel is locally constant finite type, and so is the extension, by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-derived-serre]. Apply the induction hypothesis on the current slice to obtain $L\simeq\underline E$ with $E$ a finite-module complex supported in $[a,b-1]$.

Put $n=b-1$ and $F=\underline{B^r}$. The derived boundary is now a map $\underline E\to F[-n]$. Here is its chain representative, including why it exists although the terms of $E$ need not be projective. Quasi-isomorphisms in the homotopy category admit a right calculus of fractions [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system]. By [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation], represent the map by a roof $\underline E\xleftarrow{s}T\xrightarrow{t}F[-n]$ in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism. Upper truncate $T$ at $n$; this is a quasi-isomorphism because $H^{>n}(T)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends]. The top component of $t$ kills boundaries, hence factors through $H^n(T)$. Since $H^n(s)$ is invertible, this gives $h:H^n(\underline E)\to F$. The chain map $\underline E\to H^n(\underline E)[-n]\xrightarrow{h}F[-n]$ represents the roof: after precomposition with the truncated $s$, its degree-$n$ component is exactly $t$, and all other target components are zero. Write $u:\underline{E^n}\to F$ for its top component; then $u d_E^{n-1}=0$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-morphism-local] to $u$, whose source module $E^n$ is finite, and choose a covering family contained in the resulting covering sieve, as supplied by the topology generated by the site coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Refine along this family to obtain $v:E^n\to B^r$ inducing $u$. On each nonempty slice the constant functor is faithful on module maps: if the constant sheaf of a map $f$ is zero, each element $f(x)$ has the same image as $0$ in the sheafification of the constant presheaf; local equality [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] makes these equal in that presheaf on a covering. Unless the slice is empty, that covering has a member, where its restriction is still the same element $f(x)$, so $f(x)=0$. Thus $v d_E^{n-1}=0$ from $u d_E^{n-1}=0$ (the assertion is automatic if $E^{n-1}=0$). Empty slices already have the zero model. Consequently $N=(E^a\to\cdots\to E^{b-1}\xrightarrow{v}B^r)$ is a genuine $B$-module complex supported in $[a,b]$, with every term finite.

The complex $\underline N$ is the shifted cone of the chain boundary $\underline E\to P[1]$, with the cone sign chosen so the final differential is $v$ (changing the sign of the $B^r$ component gives the alternative convention). Therefore its rotated cone triangle has the same last arrow as $P\to K\to\underline E\to P[1]$. By rotation and the morphism-of-triangles axiom [def-weil-triangulated-category] there is a comparison between these triangles that is the identity on $P$ and $\underline E$. On each cohomology sheaf the long exact sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] show the middle comparison is an isomorphism: write five consecutive terms as $A\to B\to C\to D\to E$, with $C$ the middle cohomology sheaf and the comparisons on $A,B,D,E$ identities. Work locally with sections; lifts onto images exist after covering by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], since the image is the sheafification of the presheaf image. If $c$ maps to zero in the lower $C$, its image in $D$ is zero, so locally $c$ comes from $b\in B$. The image of $b$ in the lower $C$ is zero, so locally $b$ comes from $A$, and hence $c=0$. Conversely, a section of the lower $C$ maps to $d\in D$ in the kernel of $D\to E$. Locally lift $d$ to $c$ in the upper $C$. The difference between the given section and the image of $c$ comes locally from a section $b$ of the lower $B$; adding the image of that same $b$ in the upper $C$ gives a lift of the given section. Thus the comparison is a monomorphism and locally surjective, hence an isomorphism of sheaves. Its cone is therefore acyclic, so the middle comparison is an isomorphism in the derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This proves $K\simeq\underline N$.

Compose the coverings from Steps 3, 4 and 6. The complexes $N$ (and the zero complexes on empty slices) have precisely the asserted bounds and finite terms; their differentials are induced by the displayed module maps. The base and induction step prove the claim for all $b-a\ge0$. No condition on points or a finite Tor amplitude entered the argument.
